newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Alleged drug kingpin Li Yun-chung fears for his life if sent back to jail and has asked to be extradited quickly to the United States to face drug trafficking charges there. Li was flown back from Rangoon on Saturday after jumping bail in February. He is being held in police custody and is due to appear before the Criminal Court today. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Corruption will be widespread and administrative power will be exclusively in the hands of influential and business people if the new charter is promulgated, political scientist Thirayuth Boonmi warns. Under the political structure envisaged in the new charter draft, there will be a total of 500 members of parliament of whom 400 will be directly elected under a single-MP constituency system while the remaining 100 will come from the party list. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has refused to be pinned down on the question of across-the-board pay rises for government employees. While saying that the government wants to give civil servants a wage increase, Chavalit stresses that everything depends on revenues and economic trends. He says that the Cabinet will discuss the 1998 fiscal budget at a meeting on Wednesday. (THE NATION)

- Shrimp raisers are seeking cooperation from animal feed producers to prevent the European Union from further cutting tariff privileges for shrimp imports from Thailand under its Generalised System of Preferences (GSP). The Shrimp Raisers Club may ask members of the Thai Animal Feed Association to stop importing ingredients from EU countries for animal feed for the local aquaculture industry. (BANGKOK POST)

- With high volatility in the forex market, local banks are becoming very careful with loans issued under the over-draft account, says Siam Commercial Bank president. He says his bank has exercised caution with lending under over-draft accounts during the current economic slowdown because the value of the baht against the dollar is fluctuating. (BUSINESS DAY)
